movements.name: Air Squat
points_of_performance: Feet shoulder-width apart, full foot contact
Hips descend back and down
Hip crease passes below the top of the patella (below parallel)
Maintain lumbar curve and neutral spine
Knees track in line with the toes
Complete full hip and knee extension at the top
common_faults: Loss of lumbar curve (butt wink / rounding back)
Weight shifting to toes or heels lifting off floor
Knees caving inward (valgus collapse)
Not reaching below parallel depth

scaling_options.variation: Squat to a 20-inch box/target for depth consistency
scaling_options.description: Ensures hip crease breaks parallel while maintaining balance
Relieves load to focus on torso angle and knee tracking

movements.name: Front Squat
points_of_performance: Bar rests on anterior deltoids with high elbows (rack position)
Loose fingertip grip, triceps parallel to the floor
Hips descend back and down breaking parallel
Torso stays as upright as possible
Elbows stay driven up high throughout entire ascent
common_faults: Elbows dropping down causing chest to collapse forward
Weight shifting onto toes
Gripping the bar with a full death grip instead of fingertips

scaling_options.description: Easier wrist mobility requirement while training upright torso
Reinforces anterior load balance and deep squat mechanics

movements.name: Overhead Squat
points_of_performance: Wide snatch grip on the barbell, active shoulders pushing up into the bar
Armpits face forward, elbows locked out
Barbell stays centered over the middle of the foot throughout range of motion
Hips descend below parallel with upright torso
Knees track over toes, full lockout at top
common_faults: Bar moving forward of the frontal plane
Bending elbows or soft active shoulders
Excessive forward torso lean due to ankle/thoracic tightness

scaling_options.variation: PVC Pipe Overhead Squat to 24" Box
scaling_options.description: Develops thoracic mobility and shoulder stability without spinal load
Exposes and fixes unilateral shoulder/thoracic imbalances

movements.name: Shoulder Press / Strict Press
points_of_performance: Feet hip-width apart, hands just outside shoulders
Full grip with knuckles turned upward, elbows slightly in front of bar
Core braced, glutes squeezed, ribs pulled down
Bar moves in a straight vertical path, head pulls back to clear bar
Full lockout overhead with active shoulders and head back through the window
common_faults: Hyperextending the lumbar spine (arching back to press)
Elbows flaring excessively out to the sides
Bar moving forward around the face instead of vertical

scaling_options.description: Isolates upper body pressing without lumbar compensation
Reduces shoulder impingement risk

movements.name: Push Press
points_of_performance: Dip: Hips descend straight down 2-4 inches with vertical torso
Drive: Violent, rapid hip and knee extension jumping into the floor
Press: Arms push the bar overhead only after hips reach full extension
Catch: Locked out overhead with hips and knees extended
common_faults: Muting the hips (bending forward during dip instead of vertical torso)
Pressing early before hip drive finishes
Re-bending knees upon overhead lockout (turning it into a push jerk)

scaling_options.description: Builds leg drive coordination with independent shoulder stabilizers

movements.name: Push Jerk
points_of_performance: Dip: Vertical torso dip
Drive: Powerful hip/leg drive
Drop: Catch the barbell in a partial squat with arms locked out overhead
Stand: Recover to full standing hip/knee extension before lowering bar
common_faults: Lack of full hip extension before dipping under
Soft elbow catch overhead
Lowering the bar before standing up to full lockout

scaling_options.description: Helps athletes feel the catch under the weight without barbell path constraints

movements.name: Deadlift
points_of_performance: Feet hip-width apart, bar over mid-foot
Hands outside knees with full grip
Shoulders slightly in front of the bar, lats engaged
Spine neutral, chest up
Hips and shoulders rise at the same rate until bar passes knees
Finish standing tall with hips open and shoulders behind the bar
common_faults: Rounding the lumbar spine under load
Hips shooting up first (stripper deadlift)
Bouncing bar off the floor losing tension

scaling_options.description: Allows more natural center of mass for beginners or mobility restricted athletes
Shortens range of motion to protect lower back posture

movements.name: Sumo Deadlift High Pull (SDHP)
points_of_performance: Wide stance (sumo) with toes pointed out, hands narrow on the bar inside knees
Deadlift to hips, followed by violent hip extension and shrug
Elbows pull high and outside finishing above the bar
Bar ascends to collarbone level
Arms extend back down before hips hinge on descent
common_faults: Pulling with arms before hip extension completes
Elbows dropping below the hands at the top
Narrow stance with round spine

scaling_options.description: Single implement simplifies bar path and elbow height mechanics

movements.name: Medicine Ball Clean
points_of_performance: Stance shoulder-width, ball between feet
Palms on outside of ball, arms straight, neutral spine
Deadlift to full hip extension and shrug
Pull-under into a deep front squat catching ball at chest
Stand to full extension with ball in front rack
common_faults: Curling the ball with biceps instead of dropping under
Tossing the ball up in the air
Not reaching full hip extension before pulling under

scaling_options.description: Deconstructs the hip explosion prior to adding the pull-under

movements.name: Thruster
points_of_performance: Front squat into an immediate overhead press in one continuous fluid motion
Deep squat breaking parallel with high elbows
Explosive hip extension propelling barbell off the shoulders
Full lockout overhead with ears through the window
Receive bar smoothly back into front rack while initiating the next squat
common_faults: Pausing between squat and overhead press (segmenting movement)
Dropping elbows and collapsing torso in squat
Pressing before hips fully extend

scaling_options.description: Reduces wrist and shoulder mobility demands
Lighter load emphasizing movement rhythm and conditioning

movements.name: Squat Snatch / Full Snatch
points_of_performance: Wide hook-grip stance, bar over midfoot, chest up
1st Pull: Smooth lift from floor to mid-thigh maintaining back angle
2nd Pull: Violent triple extension (ankles, knees, hips) and aggressive shrug
3rd Pull: Pull body aggressively under the bar into a deep overhead squat
Lockout: Stable overhead catch, stand to full extension
common_faults: Rushing off the floor and losing back tightness
Banging the bar out forward with hips rather than vertical trajectory
Pressing out the catch overhead instead of aggressive lockout

scaling_options.description: Removes deep overhead squat requirement while drilling hip power
Unilateral power development without complex barbell setup

movements.name: Clean and Jerk
points_of_performance: Clean: Floor to shoulders in a deep front squat with rapid elbow turnover
Stand up fully with bar in front rack
Jerk: Dip straight down, drive upward, split feet or push jerk into lockout overhead
Recovery: Front foot steps back halfway, back foot steps forward, full stand
common_faults: Catching the clean on toes with low elbows
Dipping forward on the jerk drive
Stepping back foot first on split jerk recovery

scaling_options.description: Catches both portions above parallel
Excellent conditioning scaling

movements.name: Pull-Up (Strict / Kipping / Butterfly)
points_of_performance: Full grip on the pull-up bar, arms fully extended at bottom (dead hang)
Initiate from active lats and hollow body position
Chin clearly rises above the horizontal plane of the bar
Return smoothly to full lockout at the bottom
common_faults: Not reaching full arm lockout at bottom (short-arming reps)
Chin failing to break the bar plane
Hyperextending neck reaching for the bar instead of pulling

scaling_options.variation: Ring Rows with feet at 45-degree angle
scaling_options.description: Builds horizontal pulling strength and lat engagement

scaling_options.variation: Banded Pull-Ups or Jumping Pull-Ups with controlled eccentric
scaling_options.description: Preserves vertical pulling movement pattern

movements.name: Ring Muscle-Up / Bar Muscle-Up
points_of_performance: Rings: False grip, hollow to arch kip
Aggressive hip drive up towards the rings
Fast transition: head and chest whip through the rings into a deep ring dip
Press out to full lockout on top of rings with turned-out palms
common_faults: Pulling too early before hip elevation
Missing the fast transition over the rings
Chicken winging (one elbow rolling over before the other on bar muscle-up)

scaling_options.variation: Strict Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up + Strict Ring Dip
scaling_options.description: Foundational strength prerequisite

scaling_options.variation: Low Ring Transition Drills with feet on floor
scaling_options.description: Teaches the fast turnover mechanics into the dip

movements.name: Burpee (Standard / Bar-Facing / Target)
points_of_performance: From standing, place hands on floor and kick or step feet back
Chest and thighs make contact with the floor
Press up and jump or step feet back under hips
Jump with feet leaving the floor, hands clapping overhead with full hip extension
common_faults: Chest not touching floor
Not opening hips at the jump at the top
Sagging lower back into hyperextension during the push-up

scaling_options.description: Low impact cardiovascular scaling
Reduces floor-to-stand distance for mobility or wrist limitations
